claims.statement: The how-to permits personal-account rename in FPT and GHEC; GHEC enterprise managed-user members cannot change usernames. Product wildcard availability is not universal actor permission.

GHES permissions say users with built-in authentication or LDAP can change usernames, while SSO users require the local administrator. LDAP permission is broader than DOCS-USERNAMECHANGE-1's built-in-only introduction and remains an explicit unresolved source conflict.

The prerequisite is understanding account/activity impacts through the separately reviewed username-change concept. A procedure link does not remove redirect, ownership-reference or gist/profile breakage risks.

The two settings reusables direct the user through profile-picture Settings and the Account sidebar; the shared procedure then opens Change username. UI navigation is not target authorization or evidence of change.

FPT and GHEC steps explicitly require reading warnings, confirming intent, entering a new name and changing only if available; unavailable names require another choice or suggestion. These detailed steps are not supplied in the GHES conditional branch.
The linked username reference supplies further limitations but is not reviewed by this receipt. No account rename, administrator authorization, recovery assurance or policy adoption is performed.
